transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um... I'm here because I'm having a really hard time with things at work. I teach high school, and... well, I just can't stop seeing this crooked, swollen-looking side of my face whenever I have to look at our lesson videos. 

It's really bad. Once I notice it, I can't unsee it, and I just feel like the students, the parents, the rest of the staff... I feel like they must all be staring right at it instead of actually listening to anything I'm saying.
If I were to show you a video of yourself where your face appears symmetrical to me, would you be able to accept that your face is not actually crooked?

Um... honestly, no. I don't think I could. I mean, I appreciate that you might see it that way, but... I see what I see. It's just so obvious to me. 

If you showed me a video and told me it looked symmetrical, I'd probably just think the lighting was hiding it, or... or maybe you were just trying to make me feel better. I already look at those lesson videos all the time, and the crookedness is right there. So, I don't think I could just accept it, no.
Do you find yourself spending a significant amount of time checking your face in mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?

Yeah, I do. Mirrors, definitely, but mostly it's the computer screen and the camera. Like... before I post a recorded lesson or have to join a virtual parent conference, I just get stuck. I keep changing the camera angle, replaying clips over and over, or I'll try covering parts of my face with my hand to see if it hides it. I end up re-recording the whole thing so many times that I actually miss my prep work, and... well, I end up being late with my classes because I just can't stop checking and fixing it.
How much has this preoccupation with your face interfered with your ability to maintain your teaching responsibilities or your personal relationships?

It's interfering a lot, honestly. I've really fallen behind on my lesson planning, the mentoring I do, and... and even coaching the basketball team. Because I'm spending so much time stuck on the videos and checking the camera, so much of my actual work just never gets finished on time anymore. 

It's gotten pretty serious at school. The administrators have actually started documenting my missed deadlines and some coverage problems I've caused. I'm... I'm really worried that I'm close to losing my position over this.
